review_basis: Final top-down PNG after deterministic validation round 1

review_items.concrete_reason: The west-south door opens into a vacant west lane. cabinet_dressing_south is well east of the door clearance, while bed_sleep_north and bench_dressing_foot are reached only after the natural northward turn.

Every declared target is reachable from the entry. The west lane reaches the bedside, then the open south-of-bed field connects to wardrobe_clothes_east, bench_dressing_foot, cabinet_dressing_south, and armchair_daylight_south_east without crossing another use zone.

bed_sleep_north has a long free west egress and making strip; wardrobe_clothes_east has a clear west-side dressing space; bench_dressing_foot retains a gap from the bed foot; cabinet_dressing_south has a north-side drawer zone; and armchair_daylight_south_east has an unobstructed diagonal approach.

bed_sleep_north and nightstand_sleep_west are a compact sleep group, bench_dressing_foot directly supports changing at the bed foot, and wardrobe_clothes_east plus cabinet_dressing_south make a separate two-sided clothing-storage group.

The largest masses are assigned to north, east, and south walls, leaving the west-side entrance lane and central south-of-bed field open. armchair_daylight_south_east occupies a discrete corner rather than turning the room center into a furniture cluster.

A north-wall bed with one accessible bedside surface and a bench at its foot is a normal single-occupant sleeping and dressing pattern. The wardrobe faces usable floor, and the armchair benefits from daylight while remaining outside the south window clearance.

bed_sleep_north follows the north wall, nightstand_sleep_west presents into the bedside area, wardrobe_clothes_east and cabinet_dressing_south present toward their respective operating spaces, and armchair_daylight_south_east turns toward its north-west room-facing approach rather than directly into glazing or a wall.

bed_sleep_north is visibly the primary sleeping anchor. wardrobe_clothes_east and cabinet_dressing_south establish the secondary storage frame, while bench_dressing_foot and armchair_daylight_south_east are smaller tertiary supports.

The closest bedroom_001 uses two north-side nightstands, a west-south wardrobe, no cabinet, and no armchair. This scene uses one nightstand, moves clothing storage to the east wall, adds a south-wall cabinet and south-east daylight chair, and has only the two frozen bed-nightstand edges rather than bedroom_001's three source relations.
